VoidedEvent.description:
One voided event: its key, the ground it was voided on, and how it was found.

A void de-counts every grading of one event whose committed outcome records a
different petition than the one the event was opened on. The ground is a
closed vocabulary, so nothing but that defect can be entered here, and the
entry naming it is a dated ``docs/freeze-record.md`` entry that publishes the
voided gradings' scores (``docs/process-version.md``, *Voiding an event*).

declared.description: The date of the freeze-record entry that voids it
declared.title: Declared

defect.description: The defect, as the entry states it
defect.title: Defect

detection.description: How the defect was found: `outcome-triggered` (a grading or flag on the resolved event surfaced it) or `scan` (a systematic sweep of stored docket identities, outcome-blind by construction)
detection.title: Detection

ground.description: Why the event is voided. `redocketed`: its outcome records a different petition than the one it was opened on, shown from stored docket payloads alone (docketed date, parties, lower-court number)
ground.title: Ground

description:
``src/fedcourtsai/voided_events.json`` — every voided event, append-only.

Data rather than code, so a void is a reviewed, maintainer-merged edit to one
file, and a row is never removed: removing one would re-count gradings a dated
entry withdrew.

events.description: The voided events, in the order declared
events.title: Events
